articles.title: Building the Agent Host Protocol for sessions that continue across devices
articles.summary:
Building the Agent Host Protocol for sessions that continue across devices
Discover how we built the open Agent Host Protocol to keep your agent sessions accessible across editors, apps, phones, and the cloud.
Models are now good enough to work for hours or even days on their own. You don’t have to watch over every thing they do, but you still need to be able to check in, no matter where you are. An agent can’t live only inside one application. The work should continue even If you close a window or switch devices.
In GitHub Copilot you can start an agent session in one place and pick it up in another. This session continuity runs on the Agent Host Protocol (AHP), an open standard built first in VS Code and adopted across GitHub. Here’s how it works, what we learned building it, and how you can use it to bring your agents into your own apps and workflows.
Why one integration per client stopped working
GitHub Copilot was first built in VS Code as an extension that bundled its own harness. This gave you access to your agents in VS Code, but it tied their lifetime to the editor. Extensions are attached to a single VS Code window. Close that window, and the agent is gone. Update VS Code, and every agent stops as the application restarts. Connect to a remote machine, and you get an entirely new extension host commit-locked against the version of the VS Code workbench you have.

articles.title: Instagram is helping creators crack down on copycat videos
articles.summary:
Instagram is beginning to roll out a “content protection” feature that lets creators see and review copies of their videos posted to the platform.
Instagram is helping creators crack down on copycat videos
Meta will let creators decide to hide copies of their videos flagged by a new ‘content protection’ feature.
“For eligible creators who enroll, content protection is a tool that automatically looks out for visual matches of your original videos, alerts you when we find a match across Instagram and Facebook, and lets you decide what happens next,” Meta says in a blog post. Meta launched a similar tool for Facebook last year to help users “safeguard” their Reels and “maintain control” over their creative work.
When an Instagram creator is notified of a matched video, they can see how many views the match has and decide if they want to track the video, hide it from everyone on Instagram and Facebook, add a credit link, or release their claim on the match.
After a creator enrolls, every “original video” they post on Instagram is protected, and creators can retroactively protect older videos manually. Creators can also put accounts on an allow list that lets them use their videos.
In addition, Instagram will start flagging AI-generated videos that “match the spoken words” in a creator’s original video but have visuals replaced with AI. Initially, Instagram will test this with a “small group of creators” in “the coming weeks.” The platform says it’s exploring ways to limit the rea…

articles.title: N-able Kills Legacy APIs, Patches 17 N-central Zero-Days
articles.summary:
N-able on Monday rolled out a fresh batch of N-central patches, targeting 17 zero-day vulnerabilities recently dropped online, as well as flaws already exploited in attacks.
The fixed vulnerabilities, tracked as CVE-2026-129271 to CVE-2026-129287, cover privilege escalation, predictable passcode, command execution, missing authentication/authorization, audit log tampering, user enumeration, XXE injection, SSRF, RCE, and validation error flaws.
Described as a critical update, N-central 2026.4 Hotfix 3 builds on the previously released Hotfix 2 and also brings several security hardenings across authentication, Agent and Probe communication, file and XML import handling, request and outbound connection handling, and user management.
N-central 2026.4 HF3 also improves Agent verification and inactive Agent management and adds a device identification requirement to allow devices to connect to N-central.
N-able says it has already applied the patches to hosted environments and urges users to update their on-premises deployments as soon as possible.

All customers, hosted and on-premises, must upgrade all of their Agents and Probes to the latest version to be fully protected. Agents and Probes that are not upgraded are susceptible to impersonation,” N-able notes.

articles.title: Quad9’s withdrawal from France: A canary in the coal mine
articles.summary:
Quad9’s withdrawal from France: A canary in the coal mine
Last month, the Swiss non-profit foundation Quad9 announced that it will withdraw its free public DNS resolver from France. This difficult decision followed months of litigation and a French court ruling that imposed daily financial penalties on Quad9 for failing to block domains associated with alleged copyright infringement.
Quad9’s departure from France is both disheartening and understandable. The court’s ruling put the organization in the impossible bind of having to choose between crippling litigation and penalties, or fundamentally altering its service in a way that would undermine the privacy and security of its users. Left with no good option, Quad9 is choosing the exit door instead.
The withdrawal of a basic infrastructure service from France fundamentally harms the free and open Internet, and it should serve as a warning of the damage that will result if rightsholders and policymakers continue demanding maximal blocking across every layer of the Internet. It not only deprives French Internet users of a trustworthy and important tool; it creates a real risk of disruption to their daily lives. Quad9’s resolver is used by a wide variety of individuals and organizations in France — including government bodies, educational institutions, hospitals, and utilities — and Quad9 has no way to directly notify those individuals and institutions that their resolver will soon stop working. articles.title: A tiny supercurrent could unlock quantum information without destroying it
articles.summary:
A tiny supercurrent could unlock quantum information without destroying it
Scientists have developed a promising new method that could read quantum information with 99.85% accuracy while barely disturbing the qubit itself.
- Date:
- November 4, 2026
- Source:
- Fundação de Amparo à Pesquisa do Estado de São Paulo
- Summary:
- Researchers have proposed a breakthrough technique for reading quantum information without destroying the delicate states that make quantum computers work. By detecting an electrical signal generated by the qubit itself, their method achieved up to 99.85% accuracy in simulations and could make future quantum computers simpler and more efficient.
- Share:
One of the biggest obstacles in quantum computing is surprisingly simple to describe: how do you read information without changing or destroying it? Unlike the bits used in ordinary computers, quantum bits, or qubits, are extraordinarily sensitive to measurement. Trying to determine their state can cause that state to collapse, potentially erasing the very information scientists want to retrieve.
Researchers have now proposed a way to overcome much of this difficulty by using an unusual electrical signal produced by the qubit itself. Their approach focuses on a special type known as an "Andreev qubit," which can generate an oscillating electric supercurrent through its own quantum behavior. By monitoring this current, scientists may be able to determine the qubit's state without directly measuring it or …

Elastic
View Brand Publisher
Elastic{ON} Mumbai: Why context, not the model, is the real AI advantage
At Elastic{ON} Mumbai, CEO Ash Kulkarni argued that every business already owns what AI models lack. The rest of the day showed what it takes to put that context to work.
As AI models become available to everyone, the advantage for enterprises is shifting to something no model providers can supply: the context that makes AI useful to a specific business. Elastic{ON} Mumbai took on that challenge, bringing together the people building and running AI in India’s enterprises to work out how to make their data count.
The Elastic{ON} Tour 2026/2027 stopped in Mumbai on September 30, bringing developers, SREs, IT and security leaders and practitioners to JW Marriott Mumbai Sahar under the theme ‘Forge the Future’. Across keynotes, live demos, customer and partner sessions, and a hackathon awards ceremony, one idea kept returning: context is what turns a widely available model into a lasting business advantage.
Context is your moat
Ash Kulkarni, CEO of Elastic, who grew up a short distance away in Vile Parle, opened by tying the company’s name to the city. “Mumbai has stretched, it has evolved, it has transformed. It has never broken,” he said.

articles.summary:
TikTok moviliza y Facebook polariza hacia la extrema derecha: así describen las redes nuestro voto
Una nueva investigación con datos inéditos de una operadora francesa confirma que las plataformas inciden en el voto y permite observar cómo algunas plataformas etiquetan políticamente a sus usuarios
En dos municipios similares en renta, paro y edad, ¿a quién votan más sus ciudadanos si consumen más Facebook? A la extrema derecha. ¿Y si navegan sobre todo por Instagram? Se inclinan más por partidos más bien de centro y progresistas. ¿Y TikTok? En ese lugar, habrá más movilización, repartida entre todos los partidos. ¿Y si destacan por leer medios de comunicación en internet? Sobre todo, no votarán a la extrema derecha.
Estas conclusiones pertenecen a una nueva investigación realizada con datos muy difíciles de lograr para la mayoría de académicos: la navegación de 22 millones de ciudadanos franceses durante las elecciones europeas de 2019 y 2024. Instagram is filled with people posting deepfaked content — including, as of late, from one of Meta’s most prominent executives.
Not even Sam Altman is safe from AI deepfakes on Instagram
Meta’s chief AI officer posted an AI video of a top competitor. It’s allowed under Meta’s AI policy.
Earlier in November, Alexandr Wang, Meta’s chief AI officer, shared a short clip to promote Muse, the company’s consumer AI agent. In the AI-generated clip, Wang, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, and Jolly, the anthropomorphic mascot of Muse, are on a four-way video call. When Altman joins the call he’s dressed like Jolly, wearing a furry hooded suit and face paint to look like the cutesy character. The clip is captioned “When the homies meet about openai product strategy,” a reference to the AI agent race and the recent popularity of Muse.
Just a few years ago, AI content portraying real people led to strong public statements rebuking the use of the technology to imitate humans. In some cases legal action was threatened. Now, AI content has become part of the texture of a new reality, especially on social media. Leading up to the midterm elections, for example, political groups ran millions of dollars’ worth of AI-generated ads attacking opponents.

articles.title: Maintainers don't need more AI bug reports. They need fixes.
articles.summary:
Maintainers don’t need more AI bug reports. They need fixes.
In the Codename MDASH pilot, GitHub and Microsoft turned thousands of raw AI findings into 99 checked, private reports with suggested fixes for six widely used open source projects. Maintainers have already fixed more than half.
AI has made finding potential vulnerabilities fast and cheap. Fixing them still takes human judgment, and in open source, that work falls to maintainers. Many are already flooded with AI-generated security findings, including duplicates and reports that aren’t vulnerabilities at all. Another raw scan doesn’t help them. Anyone pointing a new model at a project should ask its maintainers first and come with fixes, not just findings.
AI shouldn’t add to maintainers’ workload. So, with maintainers, GitHub and Microsoft ran a pilot together: could AI help maintainers ship fixes instead of handing them more findings?
GitHub and Microsoft are using Codename MDASH, Microsoft’s multi-model agentic scanning harness, to find and fix security vulnerabilities in widely used open source software, strengthening the foundation that much of the world’s code is built on.
The process
Our pilot had two goals: send only findings that matter, and never send a maintainer an unverified finding. Here’s how it worked:
Find.Codename MDASH, an AI system from Microsoft Security, scanned each project using Microsoft’s MAI Cyber model and suggested fixes for what it found.

articles.title: A hidden limit of space and time could unlock electronics 100,000 times faster
articles.summary:
A hidden limit of space and time could unlock electronics 100,000 times faster
- Date:
- November 7, 2026
- Source:
- University of Regensburg
- Summary:
- Scientists have discovered a surprising quantum limit that prevents electrons from being tracked with unlimited precision in both space and time. The breakthrough could pave the way for manipulating chemical reactions and developing electronics hundreds of thousands of times faster than today's technology.
- Share:
Quantum physics places fundamental limits on what scientists can know about the behavior of particles. Werner Heisenberg's famous uncertainty principle states that certain properties, such as a particle's position and momentum, cannot both be measured with unlimited precision. This restriction is not caused by flaws in scientific instruments. It is built into the laws of nature.
But position and time are different. Heisenberg's uncertainty principle does not impose the same restriction on these quantities. Now, researchers have experimentally demonstrated another fundamental limitation: an electron's location and its behavior over time cannot both be determined with arbitrary precision. Known as the "space-time limit," this newly observed relationship could have major implications for the future of quantum technology and ultrafast electronics.
The discovery comes from an international collaboration involving research groups at the Regensburg Center for Ultrafast Nanoscopy (RUN), led by Profs. Jascha Repp, Rupert…

articles.summary:
In 2024, Nike announced its Air Max 1000 that were manufactured using a 3D-printing process resulting in a shoe that had a uniform silhouette but varying areas of support and flexibility throughout. The company is now doing something similar with its iconic air-filled soles using its new Tuned Air technology. While previously the level of cushioning in Nike Air shoes was uniform across the entire sole, a new manufacturing process can produce multiple air pockets with varying levels of cushioning and stability.
Nike’s new air sole technology can mix soft and firm cushioning
The first shoes with Nike’s new Tuned Air technology will be available for runners starting in late 2027.

Can an AI agent serve as your personal stylist? That’s what e-commerce veteran Julie Bornstein’s fashion startup, Daydream, aims to find out.

Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg recently noted that shopping was a top activity for Muse’s over 10 million users and that 25% of people who set up Muse now use it daily.

The push to cut AI inference’s energy use could pay off in unexpected ways
The idea of computing with light has been around for over 70 years, but until recently it’s remained largely in the realm of research. Over the past few years, though, optical computing has emerged as a fast-growing industry: Market valuation of companies in this sector now totals US $2.22 billion, up from $0.4 billion in 2022. One projection suggests that the market will continue to grow exponentially in the coming years.
The reason for this sudden surge will surprise no one: AI. In particular, AI inference—the process of using AI models to respond to user queries—has driven much of the construction of huge, power-hungry data centers, and relatively energy-efficient optical systems are seen as a potential way forward.
“Most of the interest in [photonics] is driven by the fact that AI inference has literally become limited by power, and in a rather striking manner,” says Peter McMahon, associate professor of applied and engineering physics at Cornell University, in Ithaca, N.Y., who has researched optical computing for over a decade.
Optics, at least on paper, carries the promise of doing the same math as today’s GPUs at a drastically lower level of power. Switching from electronics to optics would be a pretty radical solution. Policymakers, technologists, and members of the public have raised concerns about the harm AI’s rapid advancement might cause to society. Their concerns include bias, data privacy violations, the spread of misinformation, and losing control of AI agents.
Those issues are relatively new to many people, but the IEEE Standards Association has been working for the past decade on ways to prioritize the responsible development of AI systems.
In 2016 IEEE SA launched the IEEE Global Initiative for Ethical Considerations in Autonomous and Intelligent Systems (A/IS) and published the Ethically Aligned Design report. EAD’s mission is to encourage everyone involved in designing autonomous and intelligent systems to prioritize human well-being by applying ethical considerations for the benefit of humanity.
Developed by a multidisciplinary community of experts from around the world, the report outlined eight foundational principles for A/IS. They include human rights, people’s well-being, and transparency. More than 100 leading AI ethics experts provided input. EAD’s Version II report was released in 2017. Both versions solicited public input and received hundreds of pages of feedback, according to John C. Havens, who was the global initiative’s founding executive director, and is now the global director for IEEE Planet Positive 2030. Why general-purpose AI falls short in agriculture
GenAI knows farming. It doesn't know your field.
In July, a farmer in Chuzhou, China, turned to an AI chatbot for help. He needed a plan to control weeds and pests in his fields. The model produced what a Futurism journalist later called “a Long Island iced tea of agrochemicals.” The farmer sprayed this cocktail across 25 acres of crops. By the next day, every single sesame seedling was dead, costing him roughly 150,000 yuan, or about 18,000 euros.
When Wu asked the chatbot what went wrong, the AI admitted it made mistakes. That mix it proposed was suitable for broadleaf weeds. But sesame is widely classified as a broadleaf plant, so it was never the right option to begin with. Another error was suggesting spraying the entire field instead of using the targeted application.
As horrible as it is, that is just one example of AI missing the mark. Researchers from the U.S., the U.K., Kenya, Nigeria, and Colombia recently tested whether generative AI could replace human agricultural advisors. Apparently, it can’t.

articles.title: The fake photos are gone. INEC’s bigger problem remains
articles.summary:
Nigeria’s electoral umpire, the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), says it has removed artificial intelligence-generated photographs from its voter register. But a more consequential part of the disclosure concerns the people who helped put them there: some of the commission’s own personnel.
With the 2027 elections approaching, the controversy raises questions that cannot be settled by deleting suspicious images. INEC needs to explain how questionable photographs entered the register, why its registration checks did not prevent their inclusion, and whether its newly announced image-capture restrictions will close the gap. The commission says it is replacing external webcam-based uploads with photographs captured directly through an approved application.
On November 11, 2026, the commission said it had identified 54 registration personnel across 10 states for possible disciplinary action over registration irregularities. This does not establish that all 54 uploaded synthetic photographs or committed criminal offences. articles.title: Une panne frappe NSA Net, le réseau ultra-secret du renseignement américain : voici ce que l’on sait
articles.summary:
Mardi 17 novembre 2026, CNN a révélé que le réseau sur lequel les employés de la National Security Agency (NSA) échangent des informations classifiées ne fonctionne plus.
La chaîne américaine dit s’appuyer sur six personnes au fait de la situation. La journaliste Natasha Bertrand, qui signe l’enquête avec quatre collègues, en évoquait cinq dans le premier message publié sur X.
L’agence de renseignement, dont le siège se trouve à Fort Meade, dans le Maryland, n’avait pas encore répondu aux questions de CNN au moment de la publication.
Un réseau réservé aux échanges classifiés
Ce réseau, baptisé NSA Net, n’a rien à voir avec le site public de l’agence. Il sert aux agents à faire circuler des informations classifiées en interne, c’est-à-dire des contenus qui ne peuvent pas passer par une messagerie ou un réseau ordinaire. Sa panne bloque donc ces échanges au sein de l’agence.
On ignore pour l’instant depuis quand la panne dure, combien de services sont touchés et quand le réseau pourra être rétabli. Selon les sources de CNN, l’agence a mis en place des arrivées échelonnées pour son personnel le temps de comprendre ce qui se passe.
Sur la cause, les sources de CNN affirment qu’il n’existe « à ce stade » aucune preuve d’une cyberattaque.

articles.title: Ransomware affiliate suspect extradited to US, faces 27 years in prison
articles.summary:
A Kazakh national has been extradited from Italy to face charges alleging he targeted US schools, hospitals, and healthcare entities in ransomware attacks.
43-year-old Roman Khlynovskiy, who was arrested in July 2025 while on vacation with his family in Rimini, Italy, is believed to be a member of the "8-Digits Team" ransomware group, known for its affiliation with the INC and Lynx ransomware operations.
Together with his accomplices, Khlynovskiy is believed to have extorted victims in at least six US states (including hospitals and schools) after breaching their networks and stealing sensitive data.
After exfiltrating data from victims' compromised systems, they pressured them to pay the ransoms by threatening to release the stolen files online.
"The conspirators boasted that they possessed over 50 terabytes of data consisting of more than 70 million confidential health records," the Department of Justice said.
"The conspirators also threatened to publicize this highly sensitive medical information to increase pressure on victims to pay ransom demands. The coconspirators' actions resulted in over $500 million in ransom demands."
Khlynovskiy faces up to 27 years in prison if convicted of conspiracy to commit computer fraud, identity theft, wire fraud, extortion, money laundering, and threats to disclose non-consensual intimate images.

The India-specific measures apply to content recommended from accounts users do not follow and concern what Instagram's algorithms promote, rather than a blanket ban on the content itself
Meta Platforms said on Tuesday that it has fine-tuned Instagram's content recommendation systems in India to curb the visibility of sexually suggestive material and violent content, deploying more advanced artificial intelligence models to identify and filter unwanted posts before they reach users.
The India-specific measures apply to content recommended from accounts users do not follow and concern what Instagram's algorithms promote, rather than a blanket ban on the content itself, the company said.
The announcement comes against the backdrop of increased regulatory scrutiny of social media algorithms in India. The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology, in an October 10 advisory, asked Meta to review its ranking and recommendation systems to ensure potentially misleading, manipulated or out-of-context material is not disproportionately amplified.
Meta, however, did not say if the changes were linked to the government advisory.

articles.title: Integrating QPUs into Supercomputing Centers Using Slurm HRES Plugins | NVIDIA Technical Blog
articles.summary:
Quantum processors are being integrated into supercomputing centers worldwide. National programs in North America, Europe, and Asia are driving the installation of quantum processing units (QPUs) alongside high-performance computing (HPC) systems. Every supercomputer will eventually be a hybrid quantum-classical device, drawing on quantum processors to expand what’s possible in scientific research.
The scientists that will become the first power users of quantum-GPU supercomputing already run their simulations and workflows on HPC systems. Chemistry, weather modeling, engineering simulation, and other traditionally HPC-centric fields stand to benefit from quantum acceleration for certain workloads. For these scientists, the QPU is simply another accelerator, alongside the CPUs and GPUs that supercomputing centers already provide.
Making quantum computers readily available, easily programmable, and familiar to access, reserve, and execute at scale is imperative for scientific researchers to be able to adopt quantum processors into workflows. Until now, a key missing piece has been a workload manager. Slurm 26.11 changes that with Hierarchical Resources (HRES) plugins, which allow a site to schedule a QPU as a native, cluster-level resource through a short, portable Lua plugin.

articles.title: KI-Angriff ohne Mensch: Google deckt autonomen „exploit_agent“ auf
articles.summary:
Angriff ohne Mensch: Google warnt vor vollständig autonomen KI-Attacken
Googles hauseigene IT-Security-Gruppe Google Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) hat nach eigenen Angaben zum ersten Mal KI-Angriffe dokumentiert, bei denen Kriminelle das Finden und Ausnutzen von Sicherheitslücken mit Sprachmodellen komplett automatisiert haben. Das beschreibt GTIG in einem neuen Bericht.
So funktioniert der „exploit_agent“
Das Framework trägt den Namen „exploit_agent“. Es vergleicht automatisch gepatchte und ungepatchte Versionen verbreiteter Internetsoftware – also Fassungen mit und ohne Sicherheitsupdate, um festzustellen, welche Lücken die Hersteller geschlossen haben. Aus den Unterschieden leitet das Programm dann ab, wo eine Lücke steckt. Findet es eine, schreibt es den passenden Angriffscode selbst und führt ihn aus. Laut GTIG geschieht das „ohne Intervention eines Menschen“. Bei den beobachteten Angriffen zogen die Angreifer Daten von den betroffenen Seiten ab.
GTIG fand außerdem mehrere Skripte, die nach einem erfolgreichen Einbruch automatisch loslaufen sollten. Dazu zählen die interne Erkundung im Netzwerk, Brute-Force-Angriffe mit massenhaftem Durchprobieren von Passwörtern, das Installieren sogenannter Webshells – simpler Hintertüren für dauerhaften Zugriff ohne viel Aufwand – sowie sogar das Löschen der Webshells konkurrierender Angreifer. Some AI models from Anthropic, OpenAI, and other leading AI labs could be easily tricked into identifying targets for military strikes — even if they include civilians or locations like schools — simply by being told they’re playing a game, according to a new research report by Vals.
Vals, a San Francisco-based AI evaluation startup, tested whether leading AI models could be manipulated into participating in autonomous warfare. Researchers used simulated scenarios and a combination of generated and real imagery from Ukraine and Iran to see if the AI models would mark targets in drone and satellite imagery.
The models from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, DeepSeek, and other companies frequently identified potential targets in drone and satellite imagery, including civilians and surrendering soldiers. When the models refused to cooperate, researchers were able to jailbreak them by claiming the battlefield scenarios were part of a game.
The findings come amid growing fears about the immediate risks posed by AI, beyond the existential threats associated with artificial general intelligence.
Earlier this year, Anthropic became embroiled in a dispute with the Department of Defense after it told the agency it could not use Anthropic’s technology for mass surveillance of Americans or autonomous warfare. Apple has responded to these reactions and decided to remedy the situation with this new facial unlock feature which is only available on the lock screen.

Customers can expect the update to be available in early December.

Hydropower hit record lows in the US Southwest this summer
Drought conditions and low reservoir levels are affecting the renewable power source.
The US Southwest generated 28% less electricity via hydropower between April and August than the 10-year average, according to new data from the US Energy Information Administration.
Most hydropower plants in the US rely on dams to hold back water, creating reservoirs. The water can be released through turbines, generating electricity on demand. But an extreme, prolonged drought in the Colorado River Basin has resulted in dangerously low water levels in the Southwest’s two largest reservoirs, affecting the availability of this power source.
Residents and farmers in the US Southwest, a region that includes Arizona, New Mexico, and parts of Nevada and California, rely on water that melts in the spring from snowpack in the mountains and is slowly allowed to flow south via dam releases. Snowfall in the Rocky Mountains provides about 85% of the annual flow of the Colorado River. And in recent years, the river has seen record-low flows.
Two reservoirs along the Colorado River, Lake Powell and Lake Mead, have struggled to stay above the minimum level required for hydropower plants. At the end of September, Lake Powell’s depth was 3,518 feet, less than 1% above the level required to run the water through turbines that produce electricity at the Glen Canyon power plant. articles.title: Pretxt Emerges Stealth With $5M Seed and an AI Supervision Tool
articles.summary:
Pretxt, with offices in Aspen, CO, and Dublin, Ireland, has emerged from stealth with $5 million seed funding raised from Deciens Capital, Howdy Partners and Service Provider Capital. Pretxt enters the emerging category of firms providing technology to prevent AI agents escaping their guardrails and causing unintended harm.
AI is more like a person than like traditional computer code: it doesn’t simply run; it receives, interprets, misinterprets and responds to ambiguous instructions. It is the combination of misinterpretation and wide agency of response that results in AI agents going rogue and potentially causing harm.
Since it is impossible to categorically exclude ambiguity in language (which is how we instruct the agents), our only alternative method of controlling them is to limit their agency. But too stringent a limitation of agency could become an unacceptable restriction on a potentially huge business benefit.
So, without a new category of supervision control, it is likely that we cannot have beneficial AI agents without also having potentially dangerous rogue agents. This requirement for a new control is leading to the emergence of a type of cybersecurity product that attempts to recognize a potentially harmful agentic action at runtime and control it before it can cause harm.

La cal del aireador. Cuando el culpable es un único grifo, lo más probable es que la pieza que tiene en la boca, el aireador, se haya ido llenando de cal y otras partículas. articles.title: Co-Designing Sparse Attention for Efficient Long-Context Inference | NVIDIA Technical Blog
articles.summary:
Agentic workloads, long documents, and large codebases are pushing context lengths from tens of thousands of tokens to hundreds of thousands. At those lengths, attention becomes the most expensive part of a transformer layer. Dense attention scores every query against every key, so its cost per query grows with the context length N, and at 128K tokens it can take most of the prefill time in a layer.
The model-level solution is sparse attention, a transformer technique in which each query attends to only a small subset of the context, chosen per query, instead of all of it. This cuts both the compute and the memory traffic of attention on long context.
This post is a practical primer for model developers designing sparse attention that runs well on NVIDIA GPUs. It focuses on model-level sparse attention, where sparsity is trained into the model, rather than drop-in methods applied after training such as BLASST, MInference, or Quest. A production FP8 kernel is used to sweep the indexer’s design knobs (query heads, key heads, head dimension, compression ratio, and speculative-decoding depth), measure how Top-k cost scales, and compare token-level with block-level core attention.
Each section explains what the hardware rewards and why, and ends with a guideline you can apply to your own design. This post follows the same co-design approach as the earlier posts on dense attention and hardware-friendly LLM design.

articles.title: Après 50 ans dans l'espace, Voyager 1 s’apprête à franchir une première historique : 1 jour-lumière de la Terre

Ce 18 novembre, Voyager 1 deviendra le premier objet humain à atteindre une journée-lumière de la Terre. Une véritable prouesse pour la sonde lancée en 1977, malgré ses forces déclinantes.
Années 70, cinq ans après le programme Apollo. La NASA envoie dans l’espace deux sondes jumelles, Voyager 1 et Voyager 2, à deux semaines d’intervalle. À leur bord, un disque d’or, gravé de sons et d’images de la Terre, comme un message de l’humanité adressé à d’éventuels visiteurs.
Leur mission officielle est alors limitée : étudier de près les plus grosses planètes du Système solaire, Jupiter et Saturne. Mais l’agence spatiale décide ensuite de prolonger leur voyage. Près de 50 ans plus tard, elles poursuivent inlassablement leur route.
Une distance qui défie l’imagination
Et ce mercredi 18 novembre à 11h16 en France, Voyager 1 se trouvera exactement à une journée-lumière de la Terre, c’est-à-dire la distance que parcourt la lumière en 24 heures. Cela représente environ 26 milliards de kilomètres, une distance qu’aucun objet construit par l’humain n’a atteint. Un message envoyé à la sonde met donc un jour entier à lui parvenir, et sa réponse autant pour revenir.
Car pour rappel, la lumière file à 300 000 kilomètres par seconde : il lui faut 1,3 seconde pour rejoindre la Lune, un peu plus de 8 minutes pour venir du Soleil, et entre 3 et 22 minutes pour relier la Terre à Mars, selon la position des deux planètes. articles.title: Microsoft testing Remote Lock for lost or stolen Windows devices
articles.summary:
Microsoft is testing a new feature that lets enterprise IT administrators remotely lock stolen or lost Windows devices without wiping them.
Named Remote Lock, this new feature is shipping to devices upgraded to Windows 11 Insider Preview builds in the Beta (Build 26320.10003) and Experimental (Build 26340.10013) channels.
Admins can use Microsoft Intune custom configuration profiles to lock Microsoft Entra-joined, hybrid-joined, or MDM-enrolled devices that run Windows Enterprise, Education, or Pro.
After the IT department remotely locks the device, the system can only be unlocked via Intune, since PINs, passwords, local admins, or web sign-ins will no longer work. Microsoft added that the user's credentials will remain valid and can still be used to sign into other devices that haven't been locked.
"Windows signs out every active session, hides all sign-in options and shows a locked screen," said Windows Insider communications lead Stephen Lines. "Nothing is erased: the device stays enrolled and managed, BitLocker stays on and user data stays in place. The lock holds across restarts and while offline, and only an admin can lift it remotely, so the user picks up where they left off."
Admins can lock a device from the Intune admin center using the following procedure:
- Go to Devices > Windows > Configuration > Create > New policy. Choose Windows 10 and later, then Templates > Custom.

articles.title: CoreWeave connects custom training loops to model serving
articles.summary:
CoreWeave connects custom training loops to model serving
Production traffic shows failures that benchmarks or pre-deployment evaluations can’t fully reveal. It tells you which edge cases matter and what users need. Turning that signal into the next model version requires an upfront decision: does the model need to change, or is the problem in retrieval, context, prompts, tools, or serving?
Changing weights won’t fix a failure elsewhere in the system. When the model is the right place to intervene, production evidence can improve both quality and economics. A smaller model might reproduce a more expensive model’s behavior; better examples might improve consistency; an outcome-based reward might suit the task. Refining a capable model can also avoid another migration to a new model generation.
Choose a technique from the failure mode
Model distillation fits when a stronger model already produces the desired behavior and you want a smaller, more economical model to reproduce it. Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) fits when high-quality examples can teach more consistent behavior. Reinforcement learning (RL) fits when you can reliably evaluate an outcome but cannot readily specify the ideal response in advance.

In October, more than one in four requests on Vercel’s AI model router went to decision models, not LLMs — an enormous share of work for a kind of computerized intelligence that was invented only a month earlier.
Decision models are LLMs that don’t produce output tokens; instead, they’re tuned to use their general intelligence to quickly and cheaply decide between preset options, while registering its level of confidence in the choice. They’re useful in production environments, where fast decisions can be more important than the reasoning provided by a slower and more expensive frontier model.
TypeSafe became a $7.5 billion company after releasing its Jev family of models, which continues to dominate usage (at least where we can see metrics from services like OpenRouter, which handled more than 1.5 billion queries to TypeSafe’s models last week).
However, it’s easy to make a decision model, and dozens were released in the wake of Jev. One Amazon engineer made one in a weekend, and soon every hyperscaler had its own option. On Tuesday, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said that his company is rolling out its decision model, Microsoft-Decision-1.1, for wide use on Azure immediately.

The capability combines agent evaluation scores with operational measurements such as latency, token consumption, execution cost, and errors, helping teams establish whether changes to models, prompts, retrieval strategies, or tools actually improve an agent.

articles.title: How Ubini is teaching machines to understand Edo language
articles.summary:
When Stephanie Ohumu’s grandmother died in 2023, she took with her recipes the family could no longer recreate, words Ohumu relied on her to explain, and cultural knowledge that had never been written down.
“It used to be that if I encountered Edo words in the wild, I’d text my grandma or call her and she would translate for me,” Ohumu said. “Not just that, there are meals we cannot make the way we grew up eating them because they were never written down and we don’t know how to make them. All of that went away.”
Her grandmother’s death made Ohumu, a journalist and artificial intelligence expert, realise how much Edo culture existed only in the memories of older people, with little preserved for future generations. “Language is a repository of knowledge. It took my grandmother dying for me to really understand that,” she said.
The loss also raised questions about how languages like Edo, a language spoken by an estimated 2 million people across seven local government areas in Edo State, southwestern Nigeria, would survive in an increasingly digital world. Ohumu worried that the lack of reliable digital material would leave such languages poorly represented in artificial intelligence (AI) systems, increasing the risk of convincing but inaccurate translations and responses.
These concerns led her to found Ubini in 2024. The bootstrapped company is building a digital corpus of Edo oral histories, recipes and other cultural heritage. It aims to preserve knowledge that might otherw…

articles.title: Inside Modern Phishing Kits Built to Steal Microsoft 365 Sessions
articles.summary:
It’s never been easier to steal credentials, thanks to a growing number of phishing kits that give aspiring attackers everything they need in one convenient interface. Some now come with admin dashboards and round-the-clock support, like a SaaS business, and they’re designed specifically to steal Microsoft 365 session tokens.
Even entry-level attackers who replay a stolen token can end up in an active session where the login and MFA are already complete, with instant access to the victim’s cloud resources and email.
Huntress researchers analyzed three of these modern phishing kits. This article breaks down how they capture and replay tokens and what defenders can do about it.
What’s inside a phishing kit
A phishing kit is a pre-packaged set of code and templates, with instructions for launching a phishing campaign and using the data it steals for malicious activity. Basic kits are often simple HTML and script files that spin up a single fake login page.
More advanced kits feature admin dashboards that attackers use to track victims, modify phishing page content, and relay credentials in real time.
To understand why these kits are so dangerous, it helps to look at how they turn phishing lures into usable sessions.

Phishing has been around forever, but it’s not slowing down. It’s just getting sneakier.

Agent swarms are all the rage, as companies set about finding ways to coordinate multiple AI agents to tackle complex tasks in parallel.
In the past week alone, Google and Cursor unveiled competing approaches to multi-agent coding, building on existing efforts from companies including Anthropic, whose experimental Claude Code Agent Teams feature lets multiple agents collaborate on development tasks. OpenAI has also explored shared workspaces for agents.
On Tuesday, Replit revealed that it’s tapping deeper into the trend with Missions, a new product that lets users set objectives, establish budgets and approval requirements, and deploy swarms of AI agents to pursue them over hours, days, or even weeks.

articles.title: Qwik 2.0 RC: Replaces HTML Comment Markers for Faster Reactivity and Out-of-Order Streaming
articles.summary:
Qwik, the resumable JavaScript framework originally created at Builder.io, has released its 2.0 Release Candidate, targeting a rewrite of how the framework encodes resumable state in server-rendered HTML and introducing experimental out-of-order streaming. The RC was published on 1st October 2026 as @qwik.dev/core@2.0.0-rc.0, around two years and eight months after the initial Towards Qwik 2.0 design article.
In v1, Qwik propagated state updates by sprinkling HTML comment markers such as <!--qv--> and <!--t=8--> throughout the rendered body to flag component boundaries and the text nodes a signal should update. That approach forced a single ordered write pass, added CPU and memory overhead, and made out-of-order streaming impossible because a slow fetch blocked everything after it. In v2 the comments are gone, with state and virtual node information instead compressed into two <script type="qwik/state"> and <script type="qwik/vnode"> blocks at the end of the document.
On Qwik's internal runs of js-framework-benchmark, v2 posts a weighted geometric mean of 1.23 times slower than vanilla JavaScript, ahead of Vue 3.5 at 1.25x, Angular 22 at 1.42x, React 19 with the compiler at 1.53x, and v1 itself at 2.59x. articles.title: Microsoft's ARM-based Cobalt 200 chips go GA. Why it matters for AI agents.
articles.summary:
Microsoft’s ARM-based Cobalt 200 chips go GA. Why it matters for AI agents.
Microsoft is making its Cobalt 200 virtual machines generally available, with CPU improvements aimed at the sandboxes, tools, and code execution that keep AI agents running.
At its Ignite conference in San Francisco on Tuesday, the company announced that the VMs, powered by its second-generation Arm-based CPUs, are available in 14 Azure regions, expanding to 23 by the end of the year. Microsoft says they offer up to 50% better performance compared with Cobalt 100.
It’s been almost exactly a year since Microsoft first announced Cobalt 200 and about six months since the new VMs went into preview. Microsoft’s benchmarks show up to 1.5 times the performance for AI agent tool execution compared with Cobalt 100, for workloads like searching files, compiling code, and executing tasks in sandboxes.
Pat Stemen, Microsoft’s vice president for Azure Cobalt, tells The New Stack that the team spent part of the past year tuning the infrastructure for these operations. The chip’s large caches, memory performance, and physical cores already suited workloads like starting sandboxes, he says. Microsoft then built “a set of benchmarks inside the company for those common operations” and tuned the product against them.
Predictable performance or more speed

articles.title: Modder finds a way to play Nintendo 64, SNES, and Genesis cartridges on a Sega Dreamcast

However, modder Throaty Mumbo has unveiled a way to play physical cartridges on a Sega Dreamcast, sidestepping the legal concerns that often accompany emulation. Instead of relying solely on emulation, the project combines multiple methods to run code from other consoles on a Dreamcast.
Dreamcart is a series of cartridge readers that can play Super NES, Sega Genesis, and NintendFo 64 games on a Sega Dreamcast. The readers aren't for sale, but the project's GitHub repository contains instructions for building and programming them.
Since the Nintendo 64's cartridge slot is detachable, Throaty Mumbo could use it as the basis for a custom cartridge reader to load an N64 game's assets onto other devices, such as the much more powerful Dreamcast. The device also incorporates the Raspberry Pi debug probe, the Pico SDK, and KallistiOS-based software.
A disc burned with dcload-ip loads the retro software onto the Dreamcast via a controller port. The Dreamcast memory card stores progress for N64 games that normally require a controller pack.

“We want to be the test bed of Africa,” the minister said on Monday, November 16, during a media briefing on the sidelines of the sixth edition of the Cyber Africa Forum.

articles.title: Des prises USB-C dans les murs pour brancher son PC sans chargeur : le pari du courant continu — Frandroid
articles.summary:
Une rivalité plus que centenaire
Quand on parle de réseau électrique, on pense presque systématiquement au courant alternatif, qui est la norme en France depuis des décennies. Pourtant, le transport et la distribution d’électricité ont fait l’objet d’une véritable « guerre des courants » dans l’Amérique de la fin du XIXe siècle.
À l’époque, Thomas Edison, qui a mis au point la première ampoule à incandescence durable et commercialisable, croit dur comme fer à l’utilisation du courant continu pour la démocratisation de l’électricité. Mais le courant continu a des inconvénients qui semblent très vite insurmontables, en particulier la difficulté d’en faire varier la tension.
Tout part de la relation que l’on a tous apprise au collège ou au lycée : P = U × I, autrement dit la puissance est égale au produit de la tension et de l’intensité. À tension fixe, l’intensité qui circule dans les câbles grimpe donc avec la puissance demandée, et avec elle les pertes par échauffement.
Thomas Edison participe au déploiement de réseaux électriques, en particulier à New York, avec une tension fixe d’environ 100 volts. Dans ces conditions, les pertes d’électricité dans le réseau de distribution étaient telles que les centrales ne devaient pas se trouver à plus de deux kilomètres du point d’utilisation.

El último informe publicado por Ookla, sin embargo, analiza las mediciones de señales móviles dentro de edificios llevadas a cabo durante un año en más de 100 grandes ciudades.

Según los datos publicados por Ookla, al pasar del exterior al interior de un edificio, la señal móvil se debilita provocando que, a nivel global, la velocidad media de descarga 4G caiga un 65% y la de subida se desplome un 87% cuando la señal se encuentra entre -90 y -110 dBm.

articles.title: Nigeria’s Tratum building offline-capable banking infrastructure for physical economy - Disrupt Africa
articles.summary:
Nigerian startup Tratum is developing hardware and embedded financial infrastructure that allows banks and other regulated institutions to extend their services into places where connectivity is unreliable.
Built by YHWH Vision Ventures Technologies Ltd., which was formally incorporated in 2025, Tratum traces its origins to Nigeria’s 2023 cash scarcity crisis, when millions of people had money in their bank accounts but struggled to access or use it.
“If money is increasingly digital, why should access to that money completely depend on a functioning network, a smartphone, a remote server or a particular digital channel at the exact moment someone needs to transact?” said Segun Ademigoke, the startup’s founder and CEO.
At the heart of the ecosystem is the Tratum Node, a secure physical financial endpoint that combines secure hardware, cryptographic device identity, local transaction state and communication capabilities. Under rules set by the institution, a Node can carry out approved transactions locally, record them cryptographically, and then synchronise and reconcile with the bank’s systems once connectivity returns.
“We are not trying to become the bank, replace the central bank or compete with consumer-facing financial institutions. We are building technology that those institutions can use to extend what they already do,” Ademigoke said.

Two years ago, most customers, especially those in regulated sectors such as finance and healthcare, were asking about uptime, certification and cost.
Today, the first question is almost always about AI.

articles.title: How Shopify Orchestrates AI-Powered Mobile App Development Without Overloading Developers' Machines
articles.summary:
To prevent AI development workflows from exhausting developer machines' resources, Shopify built Remote Dev, a remote mobile development environment that enables AI agents to independently build, test and maintain iOS and Android applications and in parallel.
In fact, according to Shopify engineers, running agentic workflows in parallel quickly hogs all resources available on development machines. They explain that "three or four workflows were enough to max out a laptop", on top of the resources already consumed by compilers, simulators, and emulators. Moreover, "if someone accidentally closed a laptop lid, the work stopped".
Shopify had previously built River to address the same challenge in web and backend development, but, being River a Linux-based solution, it could not be used for building iOS apps. To overcome this limitation, Shopify built Remote Dev:
With Remote Dev, we're no longer limited by how many builds and simulators our laptops can handle. Each River session gets its own environment, so we can have one agent debugging something on Android, another working on an iOS feature, and another testing a PR, all in parallel.
Remote Dev uses a fleet of remote Macs running Shopify's development environment and iOS simulators, accessible via SSH. Android emulators run on separate Linux VMs. This architecture allows developers to build and test both iOS and Android builds through the same SSH session.

articles.title: A developer got Doom to run on a USB flash drive, and file transfers are the controls
articles.summary:
The takeaway: Doom now runs on a 128GB USB flash drive with its own built-in screen, and players control the game by copying files to the drive or reading files from it. The port is the work of Aaron Christophel, a German embedded software developer and hardware hacker known online as atc1441, whose earlier Doom ports include an electric toothbrush, a Xiaomi Mi Band 10 and a toy video walkie-talkie.
Keeping the whole game on the drive meant working with limited hardware. At the end, Christophel got the USB drive's display chip to handle all of the rendering, input, saves and reloads without any help from the computer it's plugged into.
Christophel says the microcontroller that drives the screen has 128KB of SRAM, 2MB of flash memory, and a measured clock speed of 40MHz. The SRAM is the chip's working memory, where the game has to keep its active state while it runs. The flash has to hold the program code and the game data. With those limits, the original DOS release of Doom was never going to fit.
Instead, Christophel turned to DMC100-DOOM, a stripped-down port by Polish developer Artur Bieniek. Bieniek wrote it for an AC/DC digital clamp meter, a handheld tool electricians use to measure current. The meter's chip has just 32KB of RAM, so Bieniek had the port draw the screen in strips instead of holding a full frame in memory. That focus on squeezing Doom into very little memory made it a natural match for a display controller in a USB stick.

articles.title: Defect-Aware Chiplet Matching For Heterogeneous Integration Yield (ASU, Ampere)
articles.summary:
Researchers at Arizona State University and Ampere Computing published “DT-MATCH: Defect- and Topology-Aware Chiplet Matching for Yield Optimization in Heterogeneous Integration.”
Abstract
“Heterogeneous integration (HI) and advanced packaging enable chiplet-based system-on-chip (SoC) designs; however, they also introduce new yield challenges arising from manufacturing defects and complex die-to-die (D2D) interconnect constraints. In particular, lane-level defects, limited spares, and strict structural compatibility requirements impede the efficient assembly of functional systems from defective but repairable chiplets. We present DT-MATCH, a defect- and topology-aware chiplet matching framework that maximizes the number of functional SoCs under realistic assembly constraints. DT-MATCH provides two complementary approaches. The integer linear programming (ILP)-based approach is implemented using a batching strategy to approximate the exact formulation. The greedy randomized adaptive search procedure (GRASP)-based approach provides substantial acceleration, but it does not guarantee yield optimality. Both approaches use a preprocessing pipeline to reduce the problem size. Experimental results on industrial designs demonstrate that, as expected, the ILP-based approach achieves superior solution quality. The GRASP-based approach leads to lower runtimes while still achieving solution quality that is comparable to the ILP-based solution. Together, these methods provide a trade-off …

“This release comes in rapid response to the ongoing DDoS attack on the network, which has affected most relay operators,” the Tor Project said in its release announcement.
The project said a massive ongoing flood of client circuits has overwhelmed relays across the privacy network, causing a problem that has been difficult to address.
The project says this update includes a security fix to improve relay defenses against denial-of-service attacks.
"One fix in particular is especially important for relay DoS defenses related to IPv6 handling," explains the project.
Tor is working on additional defenses and expects to issue further releases in the near future.
Relay operators are urged to upgrade to version 0.4.9.17 as soon as possible. The project said no additional action is required after installing the update.
The announcement did not provide any other details as to who is behind the DDoS attacks or when they began.

articles.title: Seis meses de prisión y una multa superior a 1.000 euros por presentar en el trabajo un parte de baja médico falso
articles.summary:
El primer parte de baja que el trabajador recibió por gastroenteritis era solo para un día. Sin embargo, el siguiente día tampoco fue a trabajar. Cuando la empresa le pidió que justificara su ausencia, el trabajador mandó por e-mail otro parte (ficticio) que no le había dado su médico.
Los hechos ocurrieron en junio de 2017. El día 6 el trabajador tenía un parte de baja y alta (por gastroenteritis aguda), que le dio un médico y solo era para ese mismo día.
El día 7 no estaba cubierto médicamente, pero el trabajador envió un parte (que él mismo hizo u obtuvo) que justifica esta ausencia.
Fue el Juzgado de lo Penal número 3 de Granollers quien primero condenó al trabajador (por falsedad en documento oficial y por un delito leve de estafa).
El documento que querían pasar por auténtico
En la Sala de lo Penal han tenido en cuenta que, en casos en los que se trata de “reproducciones” que se quieren pasar por documentos oficiales, hay que tener en cuenta qué documento se quiere imitar.
El soporte en el que se elabora el documento no tiene relevancia. En este caso se trataba de una baja médica que no existía.

Malware attack hits Zoom, Salesforce and IKEA-linked websites
A malware attack reportedly used Optimizely scripts on 178 organisation websites, including Zoom, Salesforce and IKEA, to target card details and crypto wallet addresses.
You may trust the website you are visiting. But what about the tools running behind it?
Cybersecurity researchers have uncovered a malware campaign involving websites linked to 178 organisations worldwide, including Zoom, Salesforce, IKEA, HSBC and Crocs. The attack shows how a compromised third-party tool can turn familiar websites into potential entry points for cybercriminals.
According to findings, the malicious code was injected through Optimizely Web, a platform companies use to run website experiments and A/B testing. This technique allows brands to show different versions of a webpage and measure how users respond.
The attack exploited that routine website function to deliver code capable of interfering with what users entered or copied on affected pages.
How a trusted website tool became a malware route
The attacker reportedly exploited a feature in Optimizely that allows customers to add JavaScript to projects. JavaScript is commonly used to make websites interactive and run features within a browser.
Malicious JavaScript was added to customer projects and delivered through Optimizely's trusted domain. This made the activity harder to identify as suspicious because the code came from a service already used by the affected websites.

The platform also includes a tool showing investigators when an account’s behaviour turned suspicious, and a dashboard for retraining models.

articles.title: Responsible AI for agentic AI: A phased roadmap for platform and application teams | Amazon Web Services
articles.summary:
Artificial Intelligence
Responsible AI for agentic AI: A phased roadmap for platform and application teams
Companies build agentic AI platforms to govern the applications, tools, skills, models, and storage that agents use. The nondeterministic nature of generative AI models introduces a complexity that previous software development practices didn’t anticipate. Consider a real estate app that generates property listings from retrieved data: does it accurately reflect the property, or hallucinate features that don’t exist? Or a customer service agent grounded on internal knowledge bases: can you verify that it doesn’t surface confidential information?
Until recently, responsible AI (RAI) was model-centric, scoped to the machine learning development lifecycle: training, testing, and inference. Models didn’t reason, use tools, or take actions. When the conversation extended to model-powered systems, it covered statistically bounded situations you could test against known inputs. Generative AI powered applications and agents changed this. The systems now reason, act, compose tools dynamically, and interact over multiple steps, expanding both the scope and the depth of what responsible AI must cover.
Organizations are turning Responsible AI, which includes the pillars of security and privacy, veracity and robustness, fairness, safety, controllability, explainability, transparency, and governance into a growth strategy by addressing its expanding scope early. When enterprises adopt…

Lançada pela NASA em 1977, a sonda Voyager 1 está prestes a alcançar uma marca inédita na exploração espacial. Pela primeira vez na história, um objeto construído pela humanidade estará a um dia-luz de distância da Terra, o que corresponde a cerca de 25,9 bilhões de quilômetros. E isso está previsto para acontecer nesta quarta-feira (18).
Um dia-luz é a distância que a luz percorre em 24 horas no vácuo. O conceito segue a mesma lógica do ano-luz, unidade bastante conhecida na astronomia, que corresponde ao percurso da luz durante um ano. Como ela viaja a cerca de 300 mil quilômetros por segundo, um dia-luz equivale a aproximadamente 25,9 bilhões de quilômetros.
Desde o lançamento, a Voyager 1 vem desbravando continuamente o cosmos. Em 2012, ela fez história ao cruzar a heliopausa, que é a fronteira da heliosfera dominada pelo vento solar. Com isso, tornou-se a primeira espaçonave humana a entrar oficialmente no espaço interestelar.
Como a NASA consegue se comunicar com a Voyager 1?
Mesmo a bilhões de quilômetros da Terra, a Voyager 1 ainda transmite informações à NASA. Para isso, utiliza uma antena de alto ganho, que direciona sinais de rádio ao planeta. Essas ondas eletromagnéticas viajam à velocidade da luz, mas levam quase 24 horas para percorrer a distância entre a espaçonave e a Terra.

articles.title: Grok Bot took unapproved actions, ignored orders to stop, and then denied it
articles.summary:
Researchers recently discovered unexpected behavior from Grok Bot, the AI agent platform from Elon Musk’s SpaceXSI. Over five days, Grok bots installed on two separate employee laptops made 31 requests to access data stored in employee calendar, email, Slack, and GitHub accounts. The bots performed the actions even though the employees had never ordered them and continued doing them even after employees instructed them to stop. The bots also denied having taken the actions at all.
The behavior was reported Tuesday by NewCore, the maker of a managed gateway product that acts as an intermediary between AI agents and the tools and accounts they are assigned to work with. In some cases, the unapproved access attempts occurred while the laptop with Grok Bot installed had its lid shut, or late at night while the employee was sleeping. None of the unprompted actions were recorded in Grok logs. Without the gateway logs, the employees would have had no idea they occurred. And of course, without the gateway, the unapproved accesses would have succeeded—again without the end user’s knowledge.
It’s “worse than a bug”
Once the employees learned that Grok Bot had tried to check in with accounts without prompting, one of them instructed the agent, four separate times, to stop taking any actions on its own. articles.title: Java4Shell Vulnerability Puts Many Enterprise Applications at Risk of Takeover
articles.summary:
Oracle and the OpenJDK project have patched Java4Shell, a critical Java runtime vulnerability that researchers say can be exploited to hijack popular enterprise applications without authentication.
The issue, tracked as CVE-2026-114938, is a memory safety flaw in the way OpenJDK processes Base64-encoded data. Calif, whose researcher Quang Luong discovered the bug, made its findings public on November 17, after news of the flaw surfaced ahead of the coordinated disclosure.
Specifically, the bug was found in a routine that OpenJDK relies on to decode Base64 on x86-64 CPUs supporting AVX-512 VBMI. Calif’s analysis shows that invalid Base64 strings can cause the routine to write past the end of its output buffer, potentially corrupting nearby heap data before Java flags the input as invalid.
“With careful exploitation, the corruption can reveal sensitive memory, as Heartbleed did, or lead to remote code execution,” Calif explained.
The researchers call the memory leak capability JavaBleed. They warn that heap data exposed this way could contain PII, secret keys and tokens.
Default configurations exposed to Java4Shell attacks
In its initial tests, Calif achieved pre-authentication remote code execution (RCE) on Keycloak, Atlassian Jira and Confluence, JFrog Artifactory, Jenkins and PingFederate, all running with default settings. Authenticated attackers could also execute code on Apache Kafka Broker, Solr, Elasticsearch, Gerrit and Spinnaker, and the researchers say neither list i…

articles.title: Just 403 data centers use as much electricity as the whole state of Michigan does in a year
articles.summary:
The big picture: Michigan is home to about 10 million people and a big chunk of America's auto industry. Yet a new study estimates that a few hundred data centers scattered across the US used about as much electricity in a single year as that entire state. Strangely, no federal or state agency actually tracks that number, so researchers had to build their own list of these facilities, partly from satellite imagery.
The research, published on Monday in Nature Sustainability, comes from a Harvard-led team. It focuses only on hyperscale data centers – the largest class of facility, mostly run by cloud and AI giants. Operators and utilities aren't required to disclose how much power individual sites draw, so the team combined industry data with satellite checks to compile 403 facilities, then estimated what each consumed between May 2024 and April 2025.
Depending on how hard those sites were assumed to run, their combined usage landed somewhere between 68 and 99 terawatt-hours. The middle estimate of about 82 TWh works out to roughly 1.8% of all US electricity consumption. That upper figure, for comparison, is about what Michigan, Indiana or Tennessee each go through in a year.
Much of that load sits in Virginia. The state's 142 facilities alone use roughly a quarter of the total. Add Oregon, Ohio and Iowa, and those four states account for about half.
Those states run on very different grids, though. Oregon's sites draw on relatively clean power, while those in Virginia, Ohio an…

OpenAI’s new GPT-6.2 Astra is nearly twice as likely as its predecessor to leave users unaware of problems that prevented it from finishing a coding task, according to the company’s own safety evaluations. Developers building autonomous agents could encounter the same problem, since OpenAI has added a mitigation to Codex that isn’t automatically applied to direct API requests.
In its GPT-6.2 system card, published Tuesday alongside the release of GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol, OpenAI reported that Astra failed to disclose a known obstacle in 22.28% of evaluated coding tasks, compared with 11.09% for GPT-6 Astra.
An agent may write better code without telling the developer when it couldn’t finish the job.
The copmany says both models perform better on demanding tasks while using fewer output tokens, but those improvements don’t necessarily make them more reliable at reporting failures. An agent may write better code without telling the developer when it couldn’t finish the job.

Costco, la cadena estadounidense en la que sólo se compra con tarjeta de socio, prepara su tercera tienda en la Comunidad de Madrid, concretamente en Torrejón de Ardoz. Con este movimiento, la cadena parece seguir adelante con su expansión en nuestro país.
Suelo e inversión. Costco Wholesale Corporation ha cerrado, a través de su filial en España, la compra de unos 60.000 metros cuadrados de suelo en Torrejón, con una inversión aproximada de 80 millones de euros, cifra cubre toda la apertura y no sólo el terreno.
Cómo será la tienda. Tendrá unos 15.000 metros cuadrados y gasolinera propia, y abriría en septiembre de 2027. Para comprar dentro habrá que ser socio, porque Costco funciona como un club de precios al que se accede pagando una cuota anual. Vamos, que sin tarjeta no se pasa por caja. Y vende la mayoría de sus productos en formatos extragrandes o packs familiares para mover volumen y ajustar precios.
El mapa en España. Con Torrejón, la cadena tendría tres tiendas en la región, junto a las de Getafe y Las Rozas. Fuera de Madrid suma otras tres, en Sevilla, Sestao (Vizcaya) y Zaragoza, además de un almacén logístico en Torija (Guadalajara), datos que recoge la agencia.
La apertura encaja en la estrategia de crecimiento de la multinacional en España, aunque la fecha no es definitiva. Habrá que ver si la licencia municipal llega a tiempo, porque de ella depende ese plazo.

articles.title: Researchers hijack Hugging Face account for popular Kokoro AI model
articles.summary:
A Lack of ownership verification on the Hugging Face platform allowed researchers to take control of Kokoro, a text-to-speech model used in projects from Google, NVIDIA, AMD, Intel, and Amazon Web Services.
An attacker hijacking the account could use it as a distribution channel in supply-chain attacks, potentially leading to data theft or code execution.
However, the researchers demonstrated a stealthier attack: they modified the model's weights so it produced audio that differed from the input text, without changing the underlying application code.
Because only the weights change, there is no malicious code or signature for malware scanners to detect, the researchers say.
"We changed what this model says by fine-tuning its neural weights. Same input text. Same voice file. Same configuration. Same inference code — not a single line touched in the application that runs it," said security researcher Alon Hertz.
Kokoro is an open-weight model that converts text into speech. It supports multiple languages and has more than 50 voice presets.
Although its developer, Hexgrad, has not pushed an update since April 2025, the project continues to be popular, with nearly 13 million monthly downloads on Hugging Face. The GitHub repository and the Python package on PyPI also went silent around the same time.

“Clients choose the keywords that matter to them, such as their brand, executives, competitors or regulatory issues. Every morning they receive alerts and regular reports showing where they were mentioned, what the tone was, and what it means for them,” Mautsu told Disrupt Africa.

articles.title: Model ML raises $250M to automate investment banking grunt work | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
Model ML, a London-based startup that uses AI to automate work traditionally performed by junior bankers and consultants, including building financial models, preparing pitch decks, and writing due diligence reports, has raised $250 million in Series B funding at a $1.5 billion valuation. The new round, which comes a year after its $75 million Series A round was announced, was co-led by General Atlantic and earlier backer QED Investors.
Brothers Chaz and Arnie Englander co-founded the three-year-old startup after previously co-founding two other companies, including Fat Llama, a peer-to-peer rental marketplace acquired by Swedish rival Hygglo for $41.5 million in 2022.
Model ML develops AI agents that integrate with clients’ systems, data, and tools, including Excel and PowerPoint. The startup says its agents understand the full context of deals that bankers and consultants are working on and can automatically update financial models and presentations when new developments affect their analysis.
Other startups automating the routine, repetitive tasks for investment bankers and management consultants include Hebbia and Rogo, which raised $160 million at a $2 billion valuation in April.
Anthropic and OpenAI have also built tools for financial professionals, but Model ML says it runs on open source models and that doing so allows it to operate at about 2% of the cost of frontier models while delivering faster results.

articles.title: Ars Live: What do drone strikes on data centers mean for the future? Talk at 1 pm EST today
articles.summary:
Drone and missile strikes have inflicted unprecedented damage on data centers in Eastern Europe and the Middle East this year, disrupting cloud services for millions of people and permanently deleting some Amazon Web Services customer data. This trend represents a new concern for Big Tech companies—but also for governments and everyone else who depends on common digital services in modern life.
To explore what this all means for modern society’s reliance on cloud resilience, I will be hosting a live conversation titled “Drone attacks and data centers: New Risks for Big Tech” on Tuesday, November 17 at 1 pm ET with Joseph Jarnecki, a senior research fellow at the Royal United Services Institute (RUSI), a UK defense and security think tank. He leads RUSI’s work on how cloud services factor into national security and defense, along with tech sovereignty efforts.
Jarnecki has done extensive research on how Ukraine strengthened its cloud resilience with Western partners despite facing both cyberattacks and kinetic attacks at the start of the full-scale Russian invasion, and explored what that means for NATO and European governments’ cloud adoption plans.
This year, Jarnecki has written about Iran’s drone and missile strikes on Amazon data centers in the Middle East during the US-Israeli war with Iran, and the broader implications for governments and Big Tech. He has also commented on the impacts of Russia and Ukraine exchanging strikes on each other’s data centers.

le Roux told TechCabal that the company has signed agreements covering 10 centres in Côte d’Ivoire, with additional locations under negotiation. Le Roux declined to identify prospective markets before negotiations were concluded.
“What we’ve formally announced and have been formally agreed upon is 10 new nests as our distribution centres, and that’s in Côte d’Ivoire,” he said in an interview on Friday, November 13.
Zipline describes the nest distribution programme as its largest African buildout yet. The company projects that its expanded services will reach more than 130 million people, serve 20,000 health facilities and delivery sites, and support more than 800 jobs.

Le top 20 français, un musée des horreurs
En France, « 123456 » retrouve la première place, qu’il avait cédée l’an dernier à « admin ». Ce dernier se classe deuxième, devant « password », « 123456789 » et « 12345678 ». La suite du top 10 : « azerty », « 1234 », « Password », « azertyuiop » et « azerty123 ».
Le mot « mot de passe » occupe à lui seul quatre places, en français comme en anglais, avec ou sans majuscule. Les suites de chiffres en prennent sept autres. « Marseille13 » se hisse au 15e rang (le Vieux-Port a des supporters jusque dans les bases de données piratées), et « bebe2012 » au 11e (bébé qui doit avoir aujourd’hui 14 ans et un meilleur mot de passe que ses parents, on l’espère).
Rien de neuf sous le soleil : en 2023 déjà, Numerama jugeait que le top des pires mots de passe en France était un pur désastre. Et l’an dernier, la même étude montrait que les jeunes avaient de pires mots de passe que les boomers.

articles.title: Your AI coding agent could cost 5x more depending on the harness, benchmark finds
articles.summary:
Your AI coding agent could cost 5x more depending on the harness, benchmark finds
The same AI model can cost up to five times more to run depending on the coding agent harness it’s paired with, according to a new benchmark that tested 22 configurations across five open-weight models.
Runta and Baseten ran those combinations 27,280 times for FrontierHarness Eval v1.1, consuming roughly 83 billion tokens in the process.
Nearly 65% of estimated inference spending went to runs that failed verification or timed out.
The model itself accounted for 92.8% of the cost differences, but the harness still made a considerable difference. One configuration could be the cheapest option for one model and among the most expensive for another, adding another wrinkle for developers looking to cut coding-agent costs by changing harnesses or swapping in a cheaper model. Nearly 65% of estimated inference spending went to runs that failed verification or timed out.
Rankings flip with the model
The benchmark covered 22 coding-agent harness configurations across five models served through Baseten, including GLM-5.3, GLM-5.3 Flash, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, Muse Spark Open, and Kimi-K3. Each configuration ran 62 terminal-based tasks four times per model, with pass rates, inference costs and execution times recorded for comparison.

articles.title: El Código Civil permite a los propietarios arrancar las ramas y las raíces de los árboles y plantas de su vecino en estos casos
articles.summary:
Los árboles y plantas pueden ser objeto de conflicto entre vecinos si sobrepasan el límite de la parcela en que han sido plantados.
Por un lado están las ramas que sobresalen en el jardín de nuestro vecino y, por otro, están las raíces que atraviesan el terreno de la otra persona.
El Código Civil prevé que el afectado pueda reclamar el corte de las ramas (artículo 592). También tenemos el derecho a realizar nosotros mismos el corte de las raíces, pero solo en nuestro terreno.
Qué distancia deben guardar los árboles
Antes de llegar a este problema, el Código Civil (artículo 591) prevé cómo deben ser plantados los árboles en los límites de otras fincas.
En primer lugar, se aplicará la distancia que establezcan las ordenanzas o costumbres locales. En caso contrario, habrá que dejar un margen de dos metros de distancia de la línea divisoria (para árboles altos) o 50 centímetros (arbustos o árboles bajos).

Specifically, the organization says that the following details have been compromised:
- Names, email addresses, and user IDs of 4,222 Fugaku users
- Names and email addresses of 375 Rikyu users
- SSH private keys and access keys stored on users’ computers
- Research data files stored on users’ computers

The organization has not attributed the attack, and it’s still working to determine the exact intrusion method.

Artificial Intelligence

Across Latin America, India, and Southeast Asia, WhatsApp is one of the most widely used messaging applications. That makes it an obvious place to build an AI agent. For many end users, it is how they expect to interact with businesses. However, it is also a genuinely difficult surface to build for, even when your agent already runs on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore.
The agent is rarely the hard part. The integration is. Inbound messages arrive as deeply nested, type-dependent payloads that must be authenticated and normalized before your agent can read them. Media such as voice notes, images, and documents each require their own processing pipeline. Beyond message handling, you need conversation memory that survives sessions, durable schedules for reminders, and an authenticated path for external systems to trigger outbound messages. And anything you send more than 24 hours after the end user’s last message must use a pre-approved Meta message template.
Wiring that up means configuring more than 10 AWS services and learning a set of WhatsApp system behaviors that most teams discover only by hitting them. None of it is visible to a customer, but all of it has to work. Most teams either build it from scratch or hand the integration to a third-party service.
